overview.description: Floor tile installation for kitchens, bathrooms, entryways, mudrooms, and living areas. Includes subfloor preparation, leveling, uncoupling membranes, tile setting, and grouting.
overview.installationTime: 2-7 days depending on area and prep work

materials.name: Porcelain Floor Tile (12x12, 12x24)
materials.durability: Excellent — impervious to water, scratch-resistant, high PEI rating for foot traffic

materials.name: Wood-Look Porcelain Plank (6x36, 8x48)
materials.durability: Excellent — hardwood aesthetic with porcelain durability and water resistance
materials.maintenanceLevel: Low — requires polymer-modified thin-set and back-buttering

materials.name: Ceramic Floor Tile
materials.durability: Good — suitable for light to moderate traffic areas

materials.name: Large Format Porcelain (24x24, 24x48)
materials.durability: Excellent — seamless modern look with minimal grout lines
materials.maintenanceLevel: Low — requires precise leveling and tile leveling clips

materials.name: Natural Stone (Slate, Travertine, Limestone)
materials.durability: Good with sealing — varies by stone type, slate is most durable
materials.maintenanceLevel: High — requires sealing and periodic re-sealing

materials.name: Cement / Encaustic Tile
materials.durability: Good — develops patina over time, adds character
materials.maintenanceLevel: High — requires penetrating sealer before and after grouting

techniques.name: Schluter DITRA Uncoupling Membrane
techniques.description: Polyethylene mat with square cavities that isolates tile from subfloor movement. Prevents cracked tile over wood subfloors. Also provides waterproofing and vapor management. 1/8 inch thick.

techniques.name: Self-Leveling Compound
techniques.description: Pourable cementitious compound that flows to create a flat, level surface. Used over concrete slabs with high/low spots, old adhesive residue, or minor imperfections. Adds $2-5 per square foot.

techniques.name: Cement Board Underlayment
techniques.description: HardieBacker or USG Durock cement board over plywood subfloor. Combined subfloor + underlayment must be minimum 1-1/8 inches thick per TCNA guidelines. Seams taped and thin-set.

techniques.name: DITRA-HEAT Radiant Floor System
techniques.description: Electric heating cables set into Schluter DITRA-HEAT mat. Provides warm tile floors in cold climates. Programmable thermostat controls. Adds approximately $10-15 per square foot.

techniques.name: Tile Leveling System (Spin Doctors, Raimondi)
techniques.description: Wedge-and-clip systems that hold tile edges flush during thin-set cure. Essential for large-format tiles to prevent lippage. Clips are single-use, wedges reusable.
bestFor: open floor plans where lippage is visible

techniques.name: Crack Isolation Membrane
techniques.description: Fabric or liquid membrane applied over concrete cracks before tiling. Prevents existing slab cracks from telegraphing through to tile. DITRA also serves this function.

patterns.name: 1/3 Offset (Running Bond)
patterns.description: Each row offset by one-third the tile length. Most popular floor pattern. Natural, balanced look that hides subfloor imperfections.

patterns.name: Straight Lay (Grid)
patterns.description: Tiles aligned in a square grid. Clean, modern, simple. Requires very flat substrate — shows imperfections more than offset.

patterns.name: Herringbone
patterns.description: V-shaped zigzag pattern. Adds visual interest and movement. Popular with wood-look planks. Increases material waste by 15-20%.

patterns.name: Diagonal (45-degree)
patterns.description: Square tiles rotated 45 degrees. Makes rooms feel larger. More cuts at walls, increases waste by 10-15%.

patterns.name: Basketweave
patterns.description: Pairs of rectangular tiles alternating horizontal and vertical. Classic, historic look. Works best with smaller format tiles.

patterns.name: Versailles / French Pattern
patterns.description: Random-looking pattern using 4 tile sizes in a repeating set. Elegant, European aesthetic. Requires careful layout planning.

climateConsiderations: Radiant heated floors highly popular due to cold winters (October-April)
Freeze-thaw cycles affect unheated mudrooms and entryways — porcelain rated for freeze-thaw required
Older Boston homes often have uneven wood subfloors requiring extensive leveling
Basement moisture common — vapor management (DITRA) essential for below-grade tile
Salt and sand tracked in during winter — durable, textured tile preferred for entryways
popularStyles: Wood-look porcelain plank throughout open-concept renovations
Large format porcelain in modern Seaport and South End condos
Encaustic cement tile in Cambridge and Somerville brownstone entryways
Heated porcelain floors in master bathroom renovations
Slate and natural stone in Lexington and Wellesley colonial homes
